messages.author: 55bc554f872bd108
messages.subject: Uncertainty estimation on predicted locations
parts:
Hello Christen,
I have longitude and latitude data of N bears with some missing locations scattered through the individual trajectories. I have used the ctmm package to fit movement models for each trajectory and now I want to predict the position of bears in the missing locations. So for each trajectory, which is unique to a bear and to a single year of sampling, I have the movement model fit through ctmm and I am using predict(), to predict locations where there were NAs in the original dataset.

I want to have a measure of the uncertainty of each predicted position, and I am seeing that the predicted relocations come out with corresponding COV.x.x, COVy.y and COVx.y values. However, I am not understanding how to convert these values to an "error radius" or an axis of the "error ellipse" I can assign to the longitude and latitude coordinates imputed with predict().

Also, this might be a trivial matter, but some predicted values have additional columns, namely COV.vx.vx, COV.vy.vy and COV.vx.vy, and I can't understand why and what they mean.

Hopefully this is clear. Thank you in advance.
All the best,
Aurora

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Uncertainty estimation on predicted locations
parts:
Hi Aurora,

The COV.x.x columns are the entries of the location covariance matrix. The eigenvectors of that matrix tell you the directions of the major and minor axis of the error ellipse. The square root of the eigenvalues tell you the lengths of the 1-standard-deviation error ellipse. If you plot these predictions in ctmm, then you get the 95% error ellipses by default. The general relationship is that the number of standard deviations z == sqrt(-2*log(1-level)).

The COV.vx.vx  columns are the entries of the velocity covariance matrix, which you only get if a continuous-velocity model is selected.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Uncertainty estimation on predicted locations
parts:
Hi Aurora,

Everything internally in ctmm is in SI units (so meters). Units are converted to something easier to read only for display (with default argument units=TRUE).

Best,
Chris
